summary: Trek to Machu Picchu canceled after breaking an ankle at pickleball
story: I was due to leave for a guided trek to Machu Picchu on August 3. On July 26 I was playing pickleball at my local courts, ran back for a lob and rolled my right ankle. The X-ray showed a fracture and I am in a walking boot for six weeks. My orthopedic doctor has confirmed in writing that a four day mountain trek is out of the question. I canceled with Andes Trails on July 27. Their terms do not refund anything inside 30 days of departure, and they have confirmed that in writing. I am claiming the full cost of the tour, which I paid in March. For the record, I won the point.

items.description: Guided tour package, prepaid, not refundable

documents.name: Physician statement
documents.content: Santa Clara Valley Orthopedics, San Jose, July 27, 2026. I confirm that Mr. Daniel Cho, age 39, sustained a fracture of the lateral malleolus of the right ankle on July 26, 2026 while playing pickleball. He is in a walking boot and must avoid hiking and uneven ground for at least six weeks. He is not fit to take part in a multi-day trek departing August 3, 2026. Dr. Anita Deshmukh, Orthopedic Surgery.

documents.name: Andes Trails cancellation confirmation
documents.content: Andes Trails, July 27, 2026. Dear Mr. Cho, we confirm the cancellation of your booking AT-77120, Classic Inca Trail, August 3 to August 14, 2026, paid in full on March 28, 2026: $2,400.00. Under our terms, cancellations within 30 days of departure are not refunded. Refund due: $0.00. We wish you a quick recovery.
